note: Virtual capture-rig profiles. No real calibration was performed on this machine, therefore every profile carries calibrated=false and STRESS_UNCALIBRATED / UNCALIBRATED status. The U position moves the camera along the optical axis and re-renders; it is never simulated with resize/crop.
S10 fix.  ``max_travel_mm`` used to be 120.0 on every profile, which is the SPAN of the
three nominal lock positions (0 / 60 / 120 mm) -- not the rail's travel.  Reading it as a
travel bound made the measured u_position of 127.12 mm look like an over-travel.
The scan bench's own contract is the authority for the rail:
configs/a12/capture_contract.json, mechanics.u_axis_near_far == 'basic manual optical-axis
rail, about 150 mm, 100-200 mm reserved for adaptation' (source t052),
travel_mm_nominal = 150, travel_mm_reserved_range = [100, 200].  The same number is carried
by the rig spec synlab/degrade/specs.py: u_rail_travel_mm = 150.0 mm (DOCUMENTED, ref p530).
So the declared rail travel is 150 mm and every nominal position (0 / 60 / 120 mm) is
inside it with 30 mm of margin.  The three positions are unchanged: only the bound was
wrong.
What is NOT changed here, and why: the *enforced* per-tier limits live in
synlab/cameras/profiles.py::_TIER_SPECS (GLOBAL [-100,-40], MID [-30,30], LOCAL [40,70];
union span 170 mm) and are what transform_profile_u refuses against.  Nothing in this
repository reads ``max_travel_mm`` (0 occurrences in synlab/**), so correcting it cannot
change which positions a pipeline can realise -- it only stops the bound from
contradicting the contract.  Widening the tier windows would change the reachable working
distances and therefore the data, which is a separate decision.
Checked by tools/a12_u_travel_check.py.
